name: Route II: The River and Heartland Road

pages.name: Route II: The River and Heartland Road
pages.html:
The green route follows the Dargaard/Maelgoth corridor through the Solamnic heartland to Brasdel, Solanthus, and Garnet, then chooses a final transport branch toward Gilthanost or Zaradene.

LegNormal timeExpected window
Vogler → Dargaard country3–4 days23–24 Darkember
Dargaard → Maelgoth2–3 days25–27 Darkember
Maelgoth → Brasdel4–5 days1–3 Frostkolt
Brasdel → Solanthus2–3 days3–6 Frostkolt
Solanthus → Garnet3–4 days7–10 Frostkolt
Garnet → Gilthanost branch (A) → Wayreth8–13 days17–22 Frostkolt
Garnet → Zaradene branch → Wayreth10–15 days20–25 Frostkolt

Reading These Windows

Every window above is an arrival window for a normal journey, and each already includes the short stops described on that leg's page. They are not best-case figures. The whole-route totals below are the ones to quote at the table.

How the journey goesDays from VoglerReaches WayrethAgainst the 26 Frostkolt deadline
Fast — mounted, river-assisted, Branch A~24–2516–17 FrostkoltNine days spare
Normal — mounted25–3017–22 FrostkoltFour to nine days spare
Branch B via Zaradene28–3320–25 FrostkoltOne to six days spare
Mostly on foot31–3523–27 FrostkoltTight, and past it at the far end

Route Identity

This is the most adaptable route. Roads, river traffic, horses, cities, smiths, healers, and alternate transport all exist. Its danger is that the party travels through the part of Solamnia everyone else needs too.

If you want inns, horses, bridges and people who know which direction south is, take this one. Just do not knock on the door at Dargaard.

— Ispin Greenshield

pages.name: Leg 1: Vogler to Dargaard Country
pages.html:
The road moves toward Nightlund and the shadow of Dargaard before bending into the safer heartland corridor.

Atmosphere

Begin with ordinary Solamnic road markers and working farms. Each day toward Dargaard removes a little warmth: fewer travelers after sunset, abandoned roadside shrines, and locals who give directions without looking toward the Keep.

Road Scenes

  1. The Roadside Bell. Travelers ring a small iron bell before entering the darker stretch. Nobody agrees why.
  2. The Missing Wagon. Tracks leave the road toward old stonework. Following them is optional and costs time if pursued deeply.
  3. The First Warning. A local tells the party exactly where not to camp and refuses all payment for the advice.

pages.name: Stop 1: Dargaard Corridor — Do Not Knock
pages.html:
Dargaard should feel like a place the party is passing near, not a dungeon marker they are expected to clear.

Expected windowSuggested playPrimary function
23–24 DarkemberHalf session or optional full adventureTone, temptation, supernatural danger, route choice under pressure

Arrival

The ruined stronghold and its surrounding country dominate conversation long before the party sees anything clearly. Roads avoid direct approaches. Travelers lower their voices. Even experienced soldiers prefer daylight.

Scenes

  1. The Light in the Window. A light burns where no living household should be. Investigating is a deliberate time-risk decision.
  2. The Song on the Road. Someone hears distant singing at night. Following it leads away from Maelgoth.
  3. A Survivor. A traveler emerges from a side road with no memory of the last six hours and a black rose pinned to their cloak.

Knowledge Available

  • Dargaard is not merely an abandoned fort.
  • Locals understand that curiosity itself is dangerous here.
  • The safest route is to remain on the corridor and keep moving.

Look at Dargaard from a distance. That is close enough. Do not enter. Do not accept hospitality. Do not investigate the light in the window.

— Ispin Greenshield

pages.name: Stop 2: Maelgoth — Capital of Hinterlund
pages.html:
Maelgoth returns the party to civilization and makes clear that civilization is already mobilizing.

Expected dateSuggested playPrimary function
25–27 DarkemberHalf to one sessionFresh horses, information, Krell option, confirmation of war pressure

Arrival

Barges, wagons, officials, soldiers, and refugees all compete for the same roads and warehouses. The city is functioning, but every system is beginning to carry more weight than it was designed for.

Campaign NPCs

  • Sergeant Elira Venn: practical militia officer tracking strange enemy scouts.
  • Tomas Greybale: caravan master who knew Ispin and can price horses honestly.
  • Mira Redthread: robe-affiliated traveler who recognizes the Night of the Eye calculation.

Scenes

  1. Horse Market. Military buyers are taking the best mounts. Secure replacements now or risk worse options later.
  2. Refugee Ledger. A bureaucratic problem can be solved without combat but costs social capital.
  3. The Guarded Traveler. Krell can enter here, either under arrest, hidden in a caravan, or seeking someone named in Ispin’s papers.

Knowledge Available

  • The road to Brasdel remains open.
  • Solanthus is preparing for serious disruption.
  • Wayreth appears in different places on respected maps.

pages.name: Leg 2: Maelgoth to Brasdel
pages.html:
Four to five days through increasingly familiar Solamnic country gives the party a chance to see how ordinary people prepare for extraordinary news.

Travel Beats

  1. Shared Road. Merchants, mounted messengers, pilgrims, and militia units all move at different speeds.
  2. Broken Bridge. Repair, ford, wait for local labor, or pay for priority passage.
  3. The Empty Inn. An inn has food and fire but no proprietor. The explanation may be mundane, criminal, or supernatural depending on the campaign’s tone.

Route Benefit

A failed complication on this route can often be solved with coin, replacement transport, or a favor. That flexibility is the route’s mechanical strength.

pages.name: Stop 3: Brasdel — A Place Worth Remembering
pages.html:
Brasdel is useful because it is not a grand fortress or famous port. It lets the party experience what the war threatens to erase.

Expected dateSuggested playPrimary function
1–3 FrostkoltHalf sessionCharacter scenes, local problem, resupply without politics

Arrival

A proper inn, a working blacksmith, stable yards, farmers, traders, and people more interested in weather and livestock than the Conclave. Let the party have a meal where nobody knows they are important.

Campaign NPCs

  • Jessa Moor: innkeeper with a memory for travelers and an old unpaid Ispin tab.
  • Cal Bren: blacksmith who can repair travel gear quickly if the party helps with an unrelated local problem.
  • Oren Vale: young courier terrified of making the Solanthus road alone.

Scenes

  1. The Missing Herd. Livestock have scattered after something passed through at night; signs indicate organized scouts rather than predators.
  2. Ispin’s Tab. The amount is tiny. The stories attached to it are not.
  3. The Courier. Escorting Oren costs no extra time because he is traveling the same road and provides excellent Solanthus intelligence.

Brasdel is the sort of place adventurers forget because nobody has summoned a demon there recently. Treasure such places.

— Ispin Greenshield

pages.name: Stop 4: Solanthus — The Heartland Under Pressure
pages.html:
Solanthus is the route’s major urban set piece: fortified, important, wealthy enough to help, and busy enough that help always has a price.

Expected windowSuggested playPrimary function
3–6 FrostkoltOne full sessionKnightly politics, war intelligence, major resupply, milestone adventure

Arrival

Military preparations are visible without requiring the city to be under siege. Gate inspections, guild notices, horse requisitions, refugee queues, and anxious merchants make the war tangible.

Campaign NPCs

  • Sir Caldon Rook: Knight who respects direct answers and practical service.
  • Guildmistress Avara Dain: needs intelligence more than heroic speeches.
  • Scholar Pel Maren: can confirm lunar calculations and knows stories about the Orders of High Sorcery.

Scenes

  1. Forged Seals. Someone is using guild documents to divert supplies.
  2. Military Offer. The party can earn fast horses toward Garnet by handling a problem that lies directly on their route.
  3. The Wizard Question. A local official wants to know why Wayreth has summoned adventurers during mobilization.

Knowledge Available

  • Garnet is the best place ahead for fresh warhorses.
  • The route south can still be changed at Garnet depending on ships and crossings.
  • The Orders are not unified merely because the moons will align.

pages.name: Leg 3: Solanthus to Garnet
pages.html:
Three to four days carries the party from the great fortified city toward the decision point where transport matters more than road quality.

Road Scenes

  1. Horse Column. A military buyer offers excellent coin for one of the party’s mounts.
  2. Snow and Wool. Early cold weather catches less-prepared travelers and lets good equipment matter.
  3. The Split Dispatch. Two messages need carrying south; taking both provides information about both Garnet branches.

Time

Pressing exhausted mounts can save no meaningful time and risks losing them. This is a good place to teach that replacing horses is sometimes faster than “pushing harder.”

pages.name: Stop 5: Garnet — The Last Major Decision
pages.html:
Garnet is where Route II proves why it is the most adaptable road. The party can inspect its condition, replace mounts, and choose the best southern transport actually available.

Expected windowSuggested playPrimary function
7–10 FrostkoltHalf to one sessionMount replacement, intelligence, branch choice

Arrival

Warhorses, wool, trade traffic, and travelers from the south make Garnet an information market as much as a physical one.

Campaign NPCs

  • Hara Feld: horse trader who refuses to sell a mount she thinks the buyer will kill through stupidity.
  • Venn Caro: transport broker who knows whether a coastal vessel toward Gilthanost is actually available.
  • Brother Lest: traveler recently arrived through Zaradene who can describe the rougher northern crossing.

Branch Decision

BranchAdvantageRisk
A — GilthanostFastest if a vessel/transport is ready; better direct access to Qualinesti guidanceWaiting for a ship can erase the advantage
B — ZaradeneMore flexible if coastal passage is poor; avoids waiting for a perfect southern vesselLonger overland approach after landfall

If your horses are tired, replace them here. The Night of the Eye will remain unmoved by your emotional attachment to them.

— Ispin Greenshield

pages.name: Branch A: Garnet to the Coast and Gilthanost
pages.html:
This branch is the fastest form of Route II when transport is available immediately.

StageTime
Garnet → suitable coast/harbor3–4 days
Coastal passage → Gilthanost2–4 days
Gilthanost → Wayreth3–5 days

Play It as a Reward for Preparation

If the party cultivated transport contacts in Solanthus or Garnet, let the ship be waiting. If they ignored transport entirely, one day of searching is a fair cost.

Complications

  1. A captain will sail but refuses Krell aboard.
  2. The ship is carrying military cargo and has priority orders.
  3. An elven pilot requires the party to state their business before agreeing to the final approach.

Expected Wayreth

Approximately 17–22 Frostkolt under good road conditions.

pages.name: Branch A Stop: Gilthanost — The Heartland Meets Qualinesti
pages.html:
Gilthanost should feel different when reached from Route II: the party arrives dusty from Solamnia rather than shaped by weeks at sea.

Primary Scene

A Qualinesti official wants to know why a group traveling through militarizing Solamnia carries a summons connected to Wayreth. Their answers determine whether the final guide is offered freely, grudgingly, or after a service.

Knowledge

  • Wayreth is near only in the least useful sense of the word.
  • Elven guides can reach the region but cannot compel the Forest.
  • Another traveler asked about the same Master’s seal recently.

Time

Good diplomacy costs no extra day. A formal petition, investigation, or service can cost one.

pages.name: Branch B: Garnet to Zaradene
pages.html:
Use this branch when immediate coastal passage toward Gilthanost is unavailable or when the party values control over the timetable more than the theoretical fastest route.

Travel

The party reaches a rougher northern crossing and lands at Zaradene, then continues overland toward the Wayreth region.

Transport Questions

  • Can they take horses across, or must they acquire new mounts after landing?
  • Is the boat carrying only passengers, or also local trade?
  • Does Krell’s presence make the captain nervous enough to demand more coin or a favor?

Expected Wayreth

Approximately 20–25 Frostkolt with normal travel and competent mounts.

Zaradene has a dock. Calling it a harbor would be unnecessarily generous.

— Ispin Greenshield

pages.name: Stop 6B: Zaradene — A Dock and a Decision
pages.html:
Zaradene is intentionally smaller and rougher than the great Solamnic stops behind the party.

Arrival

After Solanthus and Garnet, the limited wharf, modest defenses, and small community make the party feel how far from the great roads they have come.

Campaign NPCs

  • Mera Tide: local boat owner who knows which roads remain passable inland.
  • Old Tannic: claims every map of Wayreth is a deliberate lie but still owns four.
  • Sel Faran: trader who can sell or rent mediocre mounts at excellent desperation prices.

Scenes

  1. A storm has damaged the only large ferry and locals need hands to repair it.
  2. A traveler insists the party crossed paths with them three days ago somewhere they have never been.
  3. A wounded messenger carries a fragment of a map that matches none of Ispin’s markings.

pages.name: Final Branch B Leg: Zaradene to Wayreth
pages.html:
Seven to eleven days overland gives the branch its cost: the party has escaped the great Solamnic roads but must now protect its own schedule.

Travel Pattern

  • First days: rough but comprehensible roads and farm tracks.
  • Middle days: fewer settlements, more conflicting directions.
  • Final days: the same Wayreth distortions appear as on every route.

Resource Check

If the party failed to secure mounts or supplies at Zaradene, this is where the decision matters. A hunt or repair scene can cost a day; good preparation avoids it.

pages.name: Route II: d12 Heartland Encounters
pages.html:
These encounters emphasize war traffic, law, infrastructure, and the advantages of having multiple ways to solve a problem.

d12Encounter
1A Knightly messenger’s horse collapses; the message is more important than the rider’s destination.
2Refugee wagons block a bridge while officials argue over priority.
3A merchant sells counterfeit travel passes using a real Solanthus seal.
4A roadside shrine has been vandalized with symbols none of the locals recognize.
5A river barge offers faster passage for one leg if the party helps load before dusk.
6A farmer has hidden military deserters in a barn and asks the party to say they saw nobody.
7A black rose lies in the road near the Dargaard corridor.
8A Red Robe and a Solamnic officer are arguing about whether arcane travel papers have legal standing.
9A mount throws a shoe miles from the nearest smith; improvisation keeps the schedule.
10A caravan master recognizes Ispin’s map and knows a different Wayreth location.
11A captured scout carries careful measurements of bridges and river depths.
12A perfectly normal village feast tempts the party to stay one extra night.

pages.name: Route II: d12 Rumors and Intelligence
pages.html:
The Heartland has the best information network of the three roads, but that means it also has the most confident misinformation.

d12Rumor
1“Dargaard’s lights have been seen three nights in a row.”
2“Maelgoth is buying every sound horse it can find.”
3“Solanthus has closed one gate to refugees.”
4“Garnet has horses enough for an army, but the army knows that too.”
5“A Black Robe is traveling south under Solamnic protection.”
6“There is a ship waiting specifically for people bound to Gilthanost.”
7“Zaradene’s wharf collapsed last winter and was rebuilt by fishermen.”
8“Wayreth moves because the Tower itself walks.”
9“No, the forest moves. The Tower simply waits.”
10“The Night of the Eye will make every spell three times stronger.”
11“Ispin once refused to enter Dargaard, which may be the wisest thing he ever did.”
12“Someone has been asking the same questions about your route one day ahead of you.”

pages.name: Route II: Road, River, and Mount Logistics
pages.html:
This route rewards preparation by letting the party replace a failed plan instead of merely suffering it.

ProblemHeartland solution
Exhausted horsesReplace or trade them in Maelgoth, Solanthus, or Garnet.
Broken wagonHire a smith, transfer to a barge, or abandon bulk cargo.
Closed bridgeFord, take local ferry, use river transport, or detour.
Short suppliesBuy almost anywhere until the final branch.
Wounded PCFind mundane healing or time to recover in a major city.
Bad informationCross-check with guilds, Knights, merchants, and multiple maps.

The cost is visibility. The more the party uses formal infrastructure, the easier it becomes for pursuers to learn where they went.

pages.name: Route II: Krell, Skaith, and Mereth in the Heartland
pages.html:
This route turns Krell into a legal and political problem as much as a magical one.

Krell

Introduce him between Maelgoth and Brasdel or in Maelgoth itself. He may be under guard, concealed among refugees, or carrying documents that are technically valid but clearly not his.

The Inspection

A Solamnic patrol is about to identify him. The party can turn him over, vouch for him, invoke Ispin, produce their invitation, or create a diversion. Every option creates a record.

Skaith

Skaith exploits bureaucracy: forged witness statements, duplicate descriptions, and a second “Krell” seen in another town.

Mereth

Mereth arranges a controlled meeting in Solanthus or Garnet and argues that the party is carrying a strategic threat through populated country.

pages.name: Route II Signature Adventure: The Light at Dargaard
pages.html:
This optional horror session exists because the party was explicitly told not to investigate.

Hook

A child from a stranded wagon has followed a light off the safe road. The party can continue south or enter Dargaard country long enough to bring them back.

Structure

  1. Track the child through increasingly wrong landmarks.
  2. Hear a song or voice using a name from a PC’s past.
  3. Find the child inside an abandoned roadside chapel, not the Keep itself.
  4. Escape without accepting an invitation from the figure waiting outside.

Time

Recovering the child before dawn costs no full day. Continuing deeper after the rescue costs one and may create a recurring supernatural consequence.

Reward

The party earns local loyalty and a piece of old arcane writing that becomes useful at Wayreth.

pages.name: Route II Signature Adventure: Solanthus — The Broken Standard
pages.html:
This is the route’s best full urban session.

Hook

Supplies are being diverted under legitimate-looking orders, and the theft is about to be blamed on refugees.

Scenes

  1. Interview guild clerks and soldiers who each possess only part of the truth.
  2. Trace forged seals to a warehouse.
  3. Discover scouts mapping roads rather than simply stealing goods.
  4. Choose whether to expose the local collaborator publicly or use them to feed false information.

Reward

Fast military horses to Garnet, reliable war intelligence, and one Knightly favor.

Time

Completed in one day while the party resupplies: no extra delay.

pages.name: Route II: Optional Adventures and Expansion
pages.html:
Route II can become the richest political road without changing its destination.

LocationAdventureCore question
Dargaard corridorThe Light at DargaardHow much time is a stranger worth when the safe advice is to keep moving?
MaelgothThe Guarded TravelerDoes the party trust law, Ispin, or Krell?
BrasdelThe Missing HerdCan the party protect an ordinary place without turning it into a battlefield?
SolanthusThe Broken StandardWho benefits from making refugees look guilty?
GarnetThe Last HorseWhat will the party sacrifice for speed?
ZaradeneThe Broken WharfWill the party spend precious hours repairing infrastructure they only need once?

pages.name: Route II Finale: The Road Runs Out of Answers
pages.html:
The Heartland Road ends by taking away the thing it has provided all campaign: reliable alternatives.

Expected Arrival

BranchNormal Wayreth window
Gilthanost branch (A) — mounted17–22 Frostkolt
Zaradene branch (B)20–25 Frostkolt
On foot, or heavy war delays — 31–35 days23–27 Frostkolt

Final Image

For weeks, every broken horse could be replaced, every bad road bypassed, every question asked of somebody in a city. Near Wayreth, a road sign points in two directions at once and both paths return to the same tree.

You cannot buy a better road once the Forest notices you.

— Ispin Greenshield
